mentl/c75312a:
The rule was going to be a labelling scheme — mark a guess as a
hypothesis. That is decoration, and Morgan cut it: the guess still steers
the next edit and still lands in the record whatever it is called. The
gate belongs on the action, not the rendering.

So: no edit, no doc entry, and no commit message asserts a cause the
artifact has not shown this turn. When a build fails and the reason is
unmeasured, the iteration's output is the next instrument. That is a
full iteration, not a failed one, and treating it as failure is what
manufactures the explanation in the first place.

Two corollaries, each paid for this session. One variable per march,
named in the report, or a failure cannot be attributed — the config
param and the value 1024 moved together and the value took the blame.
And an artifact answers nothing until its size is read: a grep over a
zero-byte file returns zero matches and means nothing, which is the
march's own "no verdict from empties" committed by hand.

Five causes were asserted and refuted across two iterations of one
defect. Every one came from reading code and reasoning forward; every
refutation came from running something; and the cheapest of those runs
was a two-second fixture that already existed.

layer per round: a resolution front the bound cut mid-climb.

two-top/c7b538e:
All six persistence sites wrote with a bare std::fs::write, which
leaves a truncated file when the process dies mid-write — routine on
Android, which kills backgrounded apps freely. A truncated profile.json
is the expensive case: it reads as no identity, the code mints a fresh
install-id, and the rivalry ledger is orphaned on both phones.

paths::write_atomic writes a .tmp sibling and renames it over the
target; a sibling is on the same filesystem by construction, so the
rename is atomic and a kill leaves the old file or the new one, never
a half. Routed: profile, settings, career ledger, room code, replay
tapes, and the panic hook's crash.log. The report named four sites;
the full-tree grep found six.

Load-side, a profile.json that exists but will not parse is now
quarantined as a .corrupt sibling and logged loudly instead of being
silently overwritten by the reminted identity — the old bytes were the
only evidence of what happened.
two-top/c7286fe:
Railpack's build layer compiled the vendor but its runtime layer never
carried the binary (custom build commands leave its rust provider not
knowing which artifact to promote — the deploy died on
./target/release/ice_vendor: No such file). A two-stage Dockerfile ends
the guessing: compile the workspace member in the rust image, ship the
one binary on debian-slim with ca-certificates for the outbound
Cloudflare call. railway.json keeps only the health check and restart
policy; the Dockerfile owns build and start.

noodles/c794efe:
Two findings behind 'choppy and laggy even on decent phones', both
main-thread, neither in the DSP.

The laggy half was arithmetic nobody had checked: Tone.now() returns
currentTime + lookAhead, so with lookAhead 0.25 every interactive
trigger — chord preview, drum pad, note audition, XY-pad ride, the send
knobs, even stop — sounded a quarter second after the finger, on every
device, while the context comment claimed previews 'fire at now'.
Interactive paths now schedule at tapTime() = Tone.immediate() + 5 ms;
the transport keeps its full lookAhead armor. The play lead drops
+0.18 to +0.1 now that the scheduler tick justifies it: Tone silently
derives updateInterval as lookAhead/2, so the worker tick that refills
the window after a jank ran at 125 ms instead of Tone's own 50 ms
default — updateInterval is pinned back to 0.05.

The choppy half was allocation churn feeding phone GC pauses, and a GC
pause past the lookAhead is an audible gap in every track at once.
Tone's PolySynth prunes an idle voice every second toward its running
active-average, which on any sparse lane tears voices down between
phrases and rebuilds them on the next trigger, forever, across all
twelve layer synths — disableVoiceGC clears the interval (pools stay
capped at maxPolyphony 4-5; an idle voice is a stopped source, a silent
subtree). And every sample drum hit built and disposed a ToneBufferSource
plus a Tone.Gain; playSampleHit now uses raw context nodes with the same
edges and gains. Receipt over an identical 75 s sparse-scene playback
(.tmp/perf-churn-long.mjs): 866 Tone buffer-source constructions and 2
mid-jam voice disposals before, 0 and 0 after, warmup identical. The
five meter analysers also park while the mixer sheet is closed — their
buffers were only ever read with it open.

Sound-neutral by receipt, not by claim: full calibrate against the
pre-change build matches every pinned table within 0.1 dB (master rows
0.8 and 0.7 dB spread), and npm run audit --program passes its meter
